Lara et al. - 2025 - A 20 m spatial reso:
**What it does:** This study develops a 20 m spatial resolution, wall-to-wall peatland extent map covering approximately 1.5 million km² of Alaska to address the limitations of existing coarse 1 km² peatland products and their associated sub-pixel heterogeneity.

**Key findings:** The map estimates that 7.3% (110,133 km²) of Alaska's terrestrial land area is peatland, with the greatest extent in boreal ecoregions (10.4%), and achieves an overall agreement of 85% validated against 2,785 ground and aerial reference points. The map distinguishes wet and moist peatland moisture classes, finding that wet and moist peatlands compose 2.6% and 4.7% of terrestrial land area, respectively, with spatial accuracy consistent across polar, boreal, and maritime ecoregions.

**Methods:** A support vector machine classifier was trained using fused Sentinel-1 dual-polarized SAR, Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, and ArcticDEM morphometric derivatives, spatially constrained by a topographic cost-function peatland suitability model, with ground-based peat cores and sub-meter image interpretation providing training and validation data.
